summary: Sweathouse Creek lookout: a tower was under construction in 1952, mid-1950s towermen appear in newspaper items, and the register dates today's steel tower to 2003.

staffing.status: seasonal lookout staff in newspaper items, mid to late 1950s

access.note: Register lists the tower as active with access mode drive (road). The brief's 'closed' is not stated by any source read. No source describes public visits.

facts.agency: Wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry, Government of Alberta

events.note: Newspaper item (1 Jan 1952): a new tower under construction at Sweathouse Creek, south of Sunset House. Completion not confirmed.
A towerman is named in an August 1955 newspaper item, which mentions his cabin and a three-room cabin at the tower.
Newspaper item on the 1955 season: only a few small fires started, and these were quickly put out.
Newspaper item (20 Nov 1958): a farming family returned to their farm from the Sweathouse fire tower.
Newspaper item (26 Mar 1959) reports a planned season as lookout after a course for tower men in Grande Prairie.
Register construction year (YEAR_CONSTRUCTED) for the present 30 m steel tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1955 newspaper gives the tower as 60 ft (18 m); the register gives 30 m (98 ft) for the present steel tower built 2003. The heights differ, so the 2003 tower is probably a later replacement, not the 1955 structure.

corrections.why: The register lists the tower as active with access mode drive. No source read says the tower is closed to the public.

notes_for_editor: Register LOCATION_VERIFIED is N (location by GPS), so the coordinates are not verified; the story does not rely on them. The 1955 and 1958-59 items come from a transcription of the Peace River Record Gazette on the Canada Lookouts site; the original newspaper was not checked. The 1958 and 1959 names are spelled differently in the transcription (Arnett, Annett); the story names no one. Staff names are left out. The 2003 versus 1952/1955 link is my inference from the height mismatch. Agency uses the alberta.ca wording because the brief's 'Alberta Wildfire' is not quoted in any source read. Brief access 'closed' is not supported; recorded as restricted.
